summary: An announcement and call for participation for an IEEE Computer Society workshop on Computer Networks at Lake Arrowhead, California, September 8 to 10, 1971. It was aimed at people newly entering the field.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC invites network users, researchers and manufacturers to an IEEE workshop at Lake Arrowhead. The meeting was designed for discussion of network systems and problems, including systems still being developed.

subtitle: An invitation to a small IEEE workshop on computer networks.

tldr.problem: As networking expanded, people entering the field needed opportunities to learn about systems and discuss their design.
tldr.mechanism: The IEEE Computer Society announced an invitation-only workshop with sessions on network systems, capabilities, hardware and management.
tldr.outcome: The workshop was intended to support focused discussion and encourage later research papers; its proceedings would not be published.

sections.title: Workshop Scope
sections.content:
The IEEE Computer Society West Coast Committee scheduled a computer networks workshop at Lake Arrowhead, California, for September 8-10, 1971. It was intended especially for manufacturers, users and researchers who had recently entered or planned to enter the networking field.

The organizers invited presentations on all aspects of computer networks, with particular interest in user communities, inter-node protocols, terminals and switching equipment, and communications technology. Presentations about early-stage systems were encouraged.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop was for people working in or joining the computer networking field. It welcomed talks about network systems, protocols, equipment and communications.

sections.title: Agenda and Discussion Format
sections.content:
The tentative agenda covered descriptions of specific systems, functional capabilities such as file transmission and remote job entry, hardware and software limitations, and network management problems. The meeting also included a panel session.

Participation was by invitation and limited to 65 people to support discussion. Presentations were expected to be short, followed by discussion and debate.
sections.plainLanguage: Sessions would cover systems, services, equipment limits and management. A small invited group would spend more time discussing ideas than listening to formal talks.

sections.title: Workshop Principles
sections.content:
The RFC includes IEEE workshop guidance: keep the group small, focus on a defined topic, and allow active researchers to discuss preliminary results off the record. The purpose was to examine competing approaches and help produce papers for later publication.

No proceedings from the workshop itself would be published. Participants were encouraged to publish important contributions afterward.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop was intended for open discussion of unfinished work. Participants could later publish their significant results, but the meeting itself would not produce public proceedings.
